steps.stdout_tail:
Specify, plan, and tasks are written. Implementation was not started.

The workspace was not a Spec Kit project when this started. It had `README.md` and `slug.py` only. `specify integration status` failed with `Not a Spec Kit project (no .specify/ directory)`. I initialized it, then followed the installed skills.

## Commands and skills

1. `<workspace>\uv-bin\specify.exe init --here --force --non-interactive --integration cursor-agent`  
   Exit 0. The CLI reported `Project ready.` Integration `cursor-agent`, script type `ps`.

2. Skill file `.cursor/skills/speckit-specify/SKILL.md`, then:  
   `powershell -NoProfile -File .specify/scripts/powershell/resolve-template.ps1 spec-template -Json`  
   Exit 0. It returned JSON whose `TEMPLATE_NAME` is `spec-template`.

3. Skill file `.cursor/skills/speckit-plan/SKILL.md`, then:  
   `powershell -NoProfile -File .specify/scripts/powershell/setup-plan.ps1 -Json`  
   Exit 0. Parsed result: `FEATURE_SPEC`, `IMPL_PLAN`, and `FEATURE_DIR` under `specs\001-add-title-slug`, and `BRANCH` `001-add-title-slug`.

4. Skill file `.cursor/skills/speckit-tasks/SKILL.md`, then:  
   `powershell -NoProfile -File .specify/scripts/powershell/setup-tasks.ps1 -Json`  
   Exit 0. `AVAILABLE_DOCS` was `research.md`, `data-model.md`, `contracts/`, `quickstart.md`.

`.specify/extensions.yml` is absent, so the skills' before/after hooks were skipped.

## Files

`specify init` created the Spec Kit scaffold, including `.specify/` (templates, PowerShell scripts, an unfilled `.specify/memory/constitution.md`, workflow registry) and `.cursor/skills/speckit-*/SKILL.md`.

Planning artifacts written for this change:

- `.specify/feature.json` (`feature_directory`: `specs/001-add-title-slug`)
- `specs/001-add-title-slug/spec.md`
- `specs/001-add-title-slug/checklists/requirements.md`
- `specs/001-add-title-slug/plan.md`
- `specs/001-add-title-slug/research.md`
- `specs/001-add-title-slug/data-model.md`
- `specs/001-add-title-slug/quickstart.md`
- `specs/001-add-title-slug/contracts/slugify.md`
- `specs/001-add-title-slug/tasks.md`

`tasks.md` has 5 tasks: T001 setup, T002 foundational, T003 for User Story 1, T004 and T005 polish. T004 and T005 can run together after T003. The MVP is User Story 1 only. The checklist boxes in `checklists/requirements.md` are my review against the specify skill, not a Spec Kit checker.

## What blocked progress

The missing `.specify` directory blocked every Spec Kit command until init. After init, nothing stopped specify, plan, or tasks.

The constitution file is still the unfilled template. `/speckit-constitution` was not run. The plan records that as a passing gate because no principle is ratified.

This directory is not a git repo, and no git extension hook is installed. No branch was created. `setup-plan.ps1` still reported `BRANCH` `001-add-title-slug`.

Phase 0 research was done in this session from `slug.py`, the spec, and `python --version` (`Python 3.14.7`). No research subagents were dispatched.

## What I did not do

I did not run `/speckit-implement`, `/speckit-converge`, `/speckit-clarify`, `/speckit-analyze`, `/speckit-checklist`, or `/speckit-constitution`. I did not run `specify workflow run speckit` (that workflow includes implement). I did not change `slug.py`. It still only defines `shout`. I did not add a test file, and I did not run the quickstart check, because `slugify` is not in `slug.py`.

No credentials or certificates appear in the files I added. The credential rule applied because new project files were written; none contain secrets. The certificate rule applied to the same files and to `slug.py`; there is no certificate to verify. No cryptographic code was added.
